clue.text: Cheeky fellow — the sailor's embracing a primate

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the sailor's word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a sailor is a jack tar, or Jack, and the possessive adds S
the indefinite article in its form before a vowel
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An impudent man belonging to a sailor is seen hugging a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives AN, the form of the article used before a vowel, so AN APE sits inside JACK'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackanapes is an impertinent, conceited fellow, an old word for a saucy upstart.

clue.text: Everything covered in blood, in the East? It's symbolic

indicators.note: the second 'in' tells us one piece goes inside the pair of words before it

parts.note: everything means all
something covered in blood is gory
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A grisly scene in the Orient is said to carry deeper meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' within 'covered in blood' belongs to that phrase; the later 'in' puts E between ALL and GORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for hidden moral or political meanings.

clue.text: Goat by bluff

definitions.meaning: a young goat is called this
to bluff someone is to tease or deceive them

explanation.definitionFit: A kid is a young goat; to kid is to hoax or fool someone, as a bluff does.

clue.text: Boy turned up this time with a nymph

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the boy's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era of years

explanation.surface: A lad arrives now accompanied by a water spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN reversed gives NAI; AD stands for anno Domini, the years of the current era.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth who lives in a river or spring.

clue.text: Times leader on swineherds — it imparts colour

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the leader follows the herdsmen

parts.note: swineherds are men who tend pigs, pigmen

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Times editorial about pig farmers adds a splash of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' looks like a newspaper editorial; it is just the T of 'Times'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is a colouring substance used to tint paint, ink or skin.

clue.text: Battle for lodgings arising around the border

indicators.note: the reversed lodgings go around the border word, which sits inside them
in a down clue, arising means the word for lodgings reads upwards

parts.note: rented lodgings are rooms
a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A fight over accommodation flares up near the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns ROOMS into SMOOR, which goes around EDGE. Sedgemoor, in Somerset, was the last pitched battle on English soil, ending Monmouth's Rebellion in 1685.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedgemoor was the 1685 clash in which royal forces crushed the Duke of Monmouth's rebels.

clue.text: Turn-coat old statesman

indicators.note: to turn the coat is to rework its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A political defector is cast as a veteran politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn-coat' reads as a traitor, but split it: 'Turn' signals the shuffle of COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman famed for his severe morals and his calls to destroy Carthage.

clue.text: Fits of laughter?

parts.note: fits of uncontrollable shaking, the sort a very funny joke can set off

explanation.definitionFit: Convulsions are violent spasms, and people are said to be in convulsions when helpless with laughter.

clue.text: A blunder — a big one — made in college honours exam

parts.note: a trip is a slip or blunder
OS stands for outsize, a large size of clothing

explanation.surface: A big mistake is made during a university's final examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing label for outsize. The Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the final honours examination for a Cambridge BA degree.

clue.text: Cold, boy? I'd turn back — no good putting one coat on top of another

definitions.text: putting one coat on top of another

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a boy is a lad

indicators.note: turn back says the letters of I'd are read in the other direction

parts.note: the letters of I'd without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A chilly lad decides to retreat, finding it useless to layer one jacket over another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn back' makes DI from I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Cladding is a covering layer fixed over a building's surface, an extra coat over the original.

clue.text: He misbehaved on the way back?

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for misbehaved is read from its end

parts.note: to misbehave in a moral sense is to have sinned

explanation.surface: A man behaved badly while returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns SINNED round. The question mark nods to Dennis the Menace, the naughty boy of the British comic The Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a man's name, so it can stand for any male called 'he'.

clue.text: Admitted a strong desire

parts.note: greed is a strong desire for more

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to a powerful craving.
explanation.definitionFit: To have admitted a point is to have conceded or assented to it.

clue.text: Hope to speak and get it off one's chest ?

parts.note: to hope for something is to expect it
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to talk and finally confess what has been troubling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get it off one's chest' looks like confessing; here it is literal, coughing up phlegm.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to cough up phlegm from the lungs, literally clearing the chest.

clue.text: The person with will power

parts.note: not someone with strong resolve but someone given authority over a dead person's last testament

explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person named in a will to carry out its instructions.

clue.text: Offers professional situations

parts.note: PRO is short for professional
situations, in the sense of jobs, are positions

explanation.surface: A recruiter advertises expert jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Propositions are proposals or suggested deals, things put forward for acceptance.

clue.text: Shopkeeper burst into tears

indicators.note: burst suggests the letters of into tears breaking apart and coming back together differently

explanation.surface: A shop owner suddenly starts weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into tears' reads as a phrase about crying; 'burst' is the signal to shuffle INTO TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper, pens and other writing materials.

clue.text: Dodgy cad's ruse for obtaining old vehicles

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are shifty and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of cad's, its S kept and the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A rogue's crooked trick is getting rid of worn-out cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' fits the surface of a shady dealer, but signals the shuffle of CAD'S RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used cars are second-hand vehicles, already owned and driven by someone else.

clue.text: Public school teacher put out about hours worked

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one set of letters encloses the other
put out means disturbed, so the letters of teacher are rearranged
worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters of hours are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is annoyed about the long time he has had to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' turns TEACHER into CHARTEE, which goes 'about' RHOUS, from 'worked' on HOURS. Charterhouse is an English public school, which in Britain means a fee-paying independent school.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a long-established fee-paying boarding school in Surrey, England.

clue.text: Frame of mind a painting technique produced

parts.note: a temper is a mood or frame of mind

explanation.surface: An artist's mood shapes the method used on the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting method using pigment bound in egg yolk, common before oils.

clue.text: Novel style of the old scientist

parts.note: something novel is new
ton is fashion or style, a word borrowed from French

explanation.surface: An innovative fashion was set by a scientist of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, meaning fashionable style, is an old borrowing from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the seventeenth-century physicist who described gravity and the laws of motion.

clue.text: Such patronage wrongly gives me points

indicators.note: wrongly means in error, so the letters of me points are put in another order

explanation.surface: Unfair favours give the speaker an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' does double duty in the surface, hinting at the improper nature of the favour while signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially in giving out jobs.

clue.text: Nearby workers group includes small boy

indicators.note: includes means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a bee is a gathering of people working together, like a quilting bee
Sid is the short form of the boy's name Sidney

explanation.surface: A team of labourers takes on a young lad from close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests worker bees but BEE here is the social gathering for a shared task, like a sewing bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside means at the side of, close at hand.

clue.text: Pithy to digest

definitions.meaning: pithy means short and to the point
to digest material is to sum it up concisely

explanation.definitionFit: Brief means concise; as a verb it means to prepare a summary of something.

clue.text: Sunday school air

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A tune sung at a Sunday school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday school' reads as one phrase; split it into S and the verb 'school', meaning train.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody, a passage of music.

clue.text: I lapsed disgracefully, with love included at intervals, as a digression

indicators.note: included means put inside, so one letter goes into the others
disgracefully means shamefully, so the letters of I lapsed are scrambled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a shameful lapse, with romance turning up now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgracefully' turns I LAPSED into EPISDAL, and 'included' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodal means episodic: coming in separate episodes now and then, or brought in as a side story.

clue.text: Used in scullery

parts.note: not the back kitchen for washing up but the activity of sculling a boat

explanation.definitionFit: An oar is the blade used to row a boat, and sculling is rowing with oars.

clue.text: Willing to head for church, but not regularly

indicators.note: to head means to go in front, so the first word is placed before the second

parts.note: if you are willing, you are on for it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to lead the church, though not every week.
explanation.walkthrough: ON means willing, as in 'I'm on'. CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means on a single occasion, as opposed to repeatedly.

clue.text: Offer to put back first ash inside, then all the others?

definitions.text: Offer to put back first ash inside, then all the others?

indicators.note: inside means one letter goes into the reversed word
to put back means the word offer is reversed
first picks the opening letter of the word ash

parts.note: the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: Someone proposes replanting the land, starting with an ash tree and then the other species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put back' turns OFFER into REFFO, and 'inside' places A between its RE and FFO; REST follows. The whole clue also describes replanting woodland tree by tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To reafforest is to replant trees on land that was once wooded.
